core.title: Write error_code values in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
core.given: A file outside the test roles contains an `error_code` (or `errorCode`) key with a string value
core.when: that file is written, changed, or checked
core.then: The `error_code` / `errorCode` value MUST be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$`.
prefer: Spell the machine error code in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE consistently (ORDER_NOT_FOUND, never orderNotFound).
Put human-readable messages in a separate field, which is not constrained.
avoid: Using any non-UPPER_SNAKE_CASE spelling for the code (for example a camelCase or lower-case one).
Mixing spellings for one condition (a non-UPPER_SNAKE_CASE spelling beside the UPPER_SNAKE_CASE one), which yields two codes for one condition.
unless: Files of the test roles are excluded.
Only the `error_code` / `errorCode` key is checked; other string values, including human-readable messages in a separate field, are out of scope.
core.why: An error code is the machine key a client branches on, so once a client does, its spelling is API surface; an inconsistent set (two spellings of one code) produces two codes for one condition that no testing reconciles because both are 'working'. The case convention itself is arbitrary; that it is uniform is not.
evidence: The stack's convention check reports no error-code-format finding on files outside the test roles.
Every `error_code` / `errorCode` value in files outside the test roles matches `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$`.
verification: A repository-wide check matches the error-code key (`error_code`, `errorCode`) in every file outside the test roles and tests its string value against `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$`; existing and new code are alike in scope.
Only the `error_code` / `errorCode` key is checked; other string values are out of scope, and human-readable messages belong in a separate field and are not constrained.
Files of the test roles are excluded; the exact classification of a file as a test file belongs to the stack's file-kind data / its checker, not to this rule.
The finding fact is observable only needs_new_observer: the check's finding output must be wired in as an activation observer before activation can key on it.

fires: A file outside the test roles contains an error-code value that is camelCase or lower-case (for example orderNotFound), whether newly written or already present.
A file outside the test roles sets the error-code key to a value that does not match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$.
A file outside the test roles contains both a non-UPPER_SNAKE_CASE and the UPPER_SNAKE_CASE spelling of the code for one condition.
doesNotFire: A file of a test role (unit, acceptance, e2e) contains an error-code value in any case.
A human-readable message field (separate from the error-code key) contains mixed-case text.
Other string values that are not under the `error_code` / `errorCode` key.

neutralityNotes: The convention is stack-neutral in substance (the source marks it as porting verbatim across realizations): the `error_code` / `errorCode` key spellings and `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$` are the error-payload contract, not stack constructs, so they stay in the core. Detector/validator/finding ids (bun_security_hygiene_detector, ERROR-CODE-FORMAT-001) and the detector's quote-literal match form are bunOnly. The exact classification of which files are test files is deferred to the stack's file-kind data / checker and recorded in core:verification (bun.json states no concrete test-file suffixes or paths). Nothing stack-concrete remains that a profile must supply, so profileRequirements is empty and no key is proposed; a future stack that spells the error-code key differently would need a new idiom-group profile key (e.g. idiom.error_code_keys).
